title: Puberty
hook: Somewhere around the start of the teenage years, a flood of hormones rewires the body, turning a child into someone capable of one day reproducing.
key_points: Puberty is the transition from childhood to a body capable of sexual reproduction.
It is driven by a surge of sex hormones — mainly estrogen in females and testosterone in males.
These hormones trigger growth spurts and the appearance of secondary sex characteristics.
It typically begins in the early teens, though timing varies widely from person to person.
content_html: Puberty is the body's switch from childhood into reproductive maturity. It doesn't happen overnight: over several years, a child's body gradually reshapes itself into an adult one capable of reproduction. The engine behind it all is a change in the body's chemical messengers — hormones.
extra_html: The process kicks off when the brain signals the body to ramp up production of sex hormones — chiefly estrogen in females and testosterone in males. These hormones drive a growth spurt and bring on secondary sex characteristics: changes in body and facial hair, voice, and body shape, along with the maturing of the reproductive organs themselves. Puberty usually begins in the early teens, but the exact timing varies a great deal between individuals and is perfectly normal across a wide range. NIH MedlinePlus's overview of puberty lays out the typical sequence of changes and the hormones behind them.

related.title: Hormones and the Endocrine System
related.hook: Your body runs a chemical messaging service: glands release hormones into the blood, and far-off organs read them like instructions — slow signals that shape growth, mood, and metabolism.

related.title: Human Reproduction
related.hook: New human life begins when two specialized cells — one egg, one sperm — combine, merging half a set of genetic instructions from each parent into a brand-new whole.

flashcards.back_html: The hormone-driven transition from childhood to a body that is physically capable of sexual reproduction, marked by growth and the development of sex characteristics.

flashcards.prompt: What drives the changes of puberty?

choices.text: A surge in sex hormones — mainly estrogen in females and testosterone in males
The shedding of childhood skin cells

flashcards.explanation_html: Puberty is set off by rising sex hormones. Estrogen drives much of female development and testosterone much of male development, reshaping the body over several years.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these is a typical feature of puberty?

choices.text: A growth spurt and the appearance of secondary sex characteristics
A permanent drop in body temperature
The loss of the ability to learn new skills

flashcards.explanation_html: Rising hormones trigger rapid growth and secondary sex characteristics — body and facial hair, voice and body changes — as the reproductive system matures.
